{"guidance":{"anti_examples":["Using depends_on for mere 'uses' relationships"],"examples":["core.Service depends_on core.IntegrationEdge (service needs an external integration)"],"sections":["## Definition
`X depends_on Y` means X requires Y to function correctly (runtime/build/operational requirement).

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- X requires Y to function correctly (runtime, build, or operational requirement).

## Do not use when
- X just uses Y optionally or incidentally (use `uses`), or X is a part of Y (use `part_of`).

## Domain / Range
- Domain: any system element (`core.Service`, `core.Pipeline`, `core.Repo`)
- Range: required element (`core.Service`, `core.IntegrationEdge`, `core.Policy`, etc)
"],"system4d":null},"presentation":{"axis_default":"parents"},"schema":"rocs-semantic-object-experiment.v0","term":{"characteristics":{"symmetric":false,"transitive":false},"description":"X benötigt Y, um korrekt zu funktionieren","group":"dependency","id":"core.rel.depends_on","labels":["depends_on"],"status":"active","type":"relation"}}

{"guidance":{"anti_examples":["Using is_a for instances/values (use `instance_of`)"],"examples":["core.Agent is_a core.Actor"],"sections":["## Definition
`X is_a Y` means X is a subtype of Y (inherits Y’s meaning/constraints); use for taxonomy only.

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- X is a subtype/specialization of Y (inherits meaning/constraints).

## Do not use when
- You mean instance/value membership (use `instance_of`) or part-whole (use `part_of`).

## Domain / Range
- Domain: subtype concept
- Range: supertype concept

{"guidance":{"anti_examples":["Using conflicts_with to express similarity (use `similar_to`)"],"examples":["core.Policy conflicts_with core.Policy (two rules cannot both hold for the same scope)"],"sections":["## Definition
`X conflicts_with Y` means X and Y cannot both be satisfied/true in the same scope (a direct contradiction or incompatibility).

## Notes
- Keep semantics crisp.
- Do not overload one relation with multiple meanings (Lucidity).

## Use when
- Two statements/constraints cannot both be satisfied in the same scope.

## Do not use when
- You mean tradeoff/choice history (track in decisions) or simple difference without contradiction.

## Domain / Range
- Domain: policies/constraints/invariants
- Range: policies/constraints/invariants
"],"system4d":null},"presentation":{"axis_default":"left"},"schema":"rocs-semantic-object-experiment.v0","term":{"characteristics":{"symmetric":true,"transitive":false},"description":"X steht im Konflikt/Widerspruch zu Y","group":"opposition","id":"core.rel.conflicts_with","inverse":"core.rel.conflicts_with","labels":["conflicts_with"],"status":"active","type":"relation"}}
